ownership_reason: Only the gold sees each byte of the data together with its 6-bit value; hops 1 and 2 size the buffer and copy the decoded octets by their count, hops 3 and 4 pass the data and the buffer along. Once the gold has skipped a byte, neither the count nor the octets tell a caller which byte it was. The gold's contract is the facade's own ('Decodes Base64 data into octets'), and in this code base URL-safe data is Base64 data: Base64.isBase64 counts '-' and '_' as characters of the Base64 alphabet; the streaming decoder Base64.decode(byte[], int, int), used by Base64InputStream.read and Base64OutputStream, maps them through DECODE_TABLE ('+' and '-' both decode to 62, '/' and '_' both decode to 63: 'This means decoder seamlessly handles both URL_SAFE and STANDARD base64'); the constructors say 'When decoding all variants can be decoded'; encodeBase64URLSafe emits them. The tests listed pin the decoding the gold shares with the streaming decoder (pad stop, skipped bytes, octet order) and pass. A one-line translation of '-' and '_' into '+' and '/' in a hop above the gold passes the existing tests but is a second implementation of the gold's per-character mapping placed outside the decoder (in the evidence the mapping is the decoder's own lookup) and leaves the gold dropping Base64 characters for every caller, so the path is still not consistent with the gold's documented contract.
